newsitem.title: UK: Gene makes for mighty mice, researchers say.
newsitem.headline: Gene makes for mighty mice, researchers say.

text.p: Deleting a single gene creates a musclebound mouse whose physiology could help scientists treat diseases such as muscular dystrophy or grow bigger farm animals, researchers reported on Wednesday.
Se-jin Lee and colleagues at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore said they had identified a new gene which they called growth/differentiation factor-8 (GDF-8).
Mice genetically engineered to lack the gene grew enormous muscles, they wrote in a letter to the science journal Nature.
"We disrupted the GDF-8 gene by gene targeting in mice. (Mice lacking the gene) are significantly larger than wild-type animals and show a large and widespread increase in skeletal muscle mass.
"Individual muscles of mutant animals weigh two to three times more than those of wild-type animals," they added.
The GDF-8 gene must control muscle growth, they concluded.
They said their findings could shed light on a variety of conditions or processes, from muscle-building during exercise, to cancer-induced wasting.
They could shed light on ways to manage muscular dystrophy or neuromuscular diseases -- and could be used to create genetically engineered farm animals that have more muscle and thus more meat.
